differential.name: Diabetic nephropathy
differential.rationale: Long‑standing type 2 diabetes with proteinuria/microalbuminuria and CKD progression is most consistent with diabetic kidney disease.

differential.name: Hypertensive nephrosclerosis
differential.rationale: Chronic hypertension and metabolic syndrome contribute to arteriolar sclerosis leading to CKD stage 4.

differential.name: Chronic glomerulonephritis (e.g., IgA nephropathy)
differential.rationale: Persistent proteinuria with gradual loss of renal function could reflect an underlying primary glomerular disease.

differential.name: Renal artery stenosis (ischemic nephropathy)
differential.rationale: Hypertension refractory to therapy and CKD may be driven by renal hypoperfusion from atherosclerotic stenosis.

differential.name: Medication‑induced nephrotoxicity (e.g., NSAIDs, ACE‑I overuse)
differential.rationale: Use of nephrotoxic agents in a patient with CKD can accelerate renal decline and anemia.
